metaDesc: A 2-day cross-province plan pairing Samut Songkhram and Ratchaburi: spend day one in Amphawa and Mae Klong, then catch Damnoen Saduak Floating Market early on day two, with real routes, timings, food stops, and detours.
keywords: Samut Songkhram Ratchaburi trip, Amphawa to Damnoen Saduak, Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, 2 day 1 night itinerary Thailand
h1:
Samut Songkhram–Ratchaburi
Amphawa to Damnoen Saduak, 2 Days 1 Night
intro: These two provinces sit right next to each other — a 20–30 minute drive apart — so Amphawa and Damnoen Saduak Floating Market pair up perfectly. Spend day one filling up on the Mae Klong–Amphawa side, sleep one night by the water, then get up a little early on day two for Damnoen Saduak while the boats are out in force, and pick off a few Ratchaburi sights on the way home. This is a plan that paces the time so you're never rushing and never doubling back.

blocks.html: Amphawa (Samut Songkhram) and Damnoen Saduak Floating Market (Ratchaburi) are only about 20 kilometres apart — roughly a 25–30 minute drive. Most people visit them separately even though they're this close, so this plan rolls them into a single 2-day, 1-night trip: a long, unhurried day one on the Samut Songkhram side, a night beside the Amphawa canal, then over to Ratchaburi on day two while the floating market is at its liveliest. The key is timing. Maeklong Railway Market, Amphawa Floating Market, and Damnoen Saduak Floating Market each have their own peak window, and if you get the rhythm wrong you'll miss the good stuff.

The main route is Bangkok → Samut Songkhram (about 1.5 hours via Rama II Road) → explore Mae Klong–Amphawa → overnight in Amphawa → Damnoen Saduak, Ratchaburi → a few Ratchaburi stops on the way → back to Bangkok. The trip is easiest if you drive yourself, because the sights are spread out and Damnoen Saduak Floating Market has to be done early — public transport makes the timing a headache. If you don't have a car, hire a private one or use Grab around the area in stretches.

items: Amphawa → Damnoen Saduak distance — about 20 km, a 25–30 minute drive past coconut groves and canal-side orchards the whole way
Parking — both Amphawa and Damnoen Saduak have private lots, around ฿30–100 per car; the Damnoen Saduak lots fill up fast on weekends
Market hours — Amphawa Floating Market is busiest afternoon to evening (Fri–Sun), while Damnoen Saduak has the most boats in the morning before 10am
Best season — Nov–Feb is cool and comfortable; the Amphawa fireflies show up clearest from the rainy season into early winter

blocks.title: Pick the right day
blocks.html: Amphawa Floating Market only runs Friday–Saturday–Sunday, while Damnoen Saduak is open daily but has the most boats on Saturday and Sunday. To catch both at full swing, stay over on a Saturday night and hit Damnoen Saduak first thing Sunday morning.

Day one is all on the Samut Songkhram side. Start at the Maeklong Railway Market in the morning, take in a riverside temple, then head to Amphawa in the afternoon and finish with an evening firefly boat ride.

items.activity: Maeklong Railway Market (the market on the train tracks)
items.note: Watch the vendors pull back their awnings as the train rolls in. Check the train schedule first — there are usually several runs a day — and go early when it's less crowded.

items.activity: Wat Phet Samut Worawihan (Luang Pho Ban Laem)
items.note: Mae Klong's guardian temple, close to the railway market and walkable from there
The short, bent-necked Mae Klong mackerel (pla tu) is the local specialty; there are plenty of riverside spots

items.activity: Check in by the Amphawa canal
items.note: Drop your bags, then wander the Amphawa market as the stalls start setting up

items.activity: King Rama II Memorial Park and Wat Amphawan Chetiyaram
items.note: A botanical park and canal-side museum, right next to Amphawa market and walkable

items.activity: Eat your way through Amphawa Floating Market
items.note: The canal-side food packs in around evening — grilled seafood, Thai sweets, coffee, the lot
Boats leave from the pier in the market, around ฿60–80 per person or charter the whole boat; clearest from the rainy season into early winter

blocks.title: On where to stay
blocks.html: Amphawa canal-side homestays sell out fast on weekend nights. If you're going on a Saturday, book several weeks ahead. For somewhere quieter, pick a stay over on the Bang Khonthi side or just outside the market.

blocks.text: Day 2 — over to Damnoen Saduak, Ratchaburi

blocks.html: The morning of day two is the heart of the cross-province trip. Get up a bit early and drive from Amphawa to Damnoen Saduak in about half an hour, aiming to reach the floating market before 9am when there are plenty of paddle boats selling and the sun isn't fierce yet. After that, work through the Ratchaburi stops one by one on the way home.

items.activity: Leave Amphawa, head for Damnoen Saduak
items.note: About 20 km, a 25–30 minute drive past pretty coconut groves and canal-side orchards

items.activity: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market (Khlong Ton Khem)
items.note: Go early when the paddle boats selling fruit and boat noodles are out in force. Open roughly 06:00–12:00, busiest in the morning; skip the late hours when it's packed and hot.

items.activity: Lao Tak Lak Floating Market (the old Damnoen Saduak market)
items.note: Ratchaburi's first original floating market, at the mouth of Khlong Lat Phli — quieter and more local than the main side
In Phaeng Phuai sub-district along the Bang Phae–Damnoen Saduak road; a huge main hall, an easy temple stop on the way
The Damnoen Saduak–Bang Phae area has several long-running boat-noodle shops

items.activity: Pick up Ratchaburi souvenirs — dragon-pattern jars
items.note: Ratchaburi town has ceramic shops and dragon-pattern water jars (ong) to choose from before you run back into Bangkok

blocks.title: About the boats at Damnoen Saduak
blocks.html: At Damnoen Saduak, touts will offer you a boat ride right from the parking lot. Ask the price clearly before getting on, because there are both private charters and shared boats and the prices differ a lot. If you only want to walk the canal, take photos, and eat, you can have a fine time without getting on a boat at all.

blocks.text: Tweak the plan to your style

blocks.html: The main plan above leans on floating markets and temples. If you want to add something else, here are options you can slot in without much backtracking.

items.name: Nature and mountains
items.blurb: Extend day two out to Suan Phueng for grasslands and the sheep–alpaca farms, but it's about 1.5 hours further, so plan for 3 days

items.name: Cafe and chill
items.blurb: Amphawa and the Mae Klong riverside have plenty of waterside cafes — add time sipping coffee with a canal view instead of cramming in more sights

items.name: Temples and merit-making
items.blurb: Add Wat Bang Kung with its bodhi-tree-wrapped chapel in Bang Khonthi, plus several Mae Klong riverside temples you can reach by crossing the bridge from Amphawa

items: 1 night in Amphawa — canal-side homestays from around ฿800–1,500, nicer resorts around ฿1,500–3,000
Food for 2 days — about ฿500–900 per person, cheaper if you stick to floating-market street food
Firefly boat + Damnoen Saduak boat — around ฿150–400 per person total, depending on charter or shared
Fuel + tolls + parking — roughly ฿700–1,000 per car for the Bangkok round trip

blocks.html: All in, this 2-day, 1-night trip comes to around ฿1,500–2,500 per person if you go as a group and split the lodging and fuel — good value for a near-Bangkok trip that covers two provinces.

faq.q: How far is Amphawa from Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, and how long does it take?
faq.a: Very close — about 20 kilometres, roughly a 25–30 minute drive past coconut groves and canal-side orchards the whole way, so it's easy to pair both in one trip.

faq.q: What time should I go to Damnoen Saduak Floating Market?
faq.a: Go early, before 9–10am, because the paddle boats selling fruit and boat noodles are out in force in the morning, the weather isn't hot yet, and the crowds haven't built up. The market opens around 6am and runs to noon.

faq.q: Which days are Amphawa and Damnoen Saduak floating markets open?
faq.a: Amphawa Floating Market only opens Friday–Saturday–Sunday and is busiest from afternoon into the evening, while Damnoen Saduak is open daily but has the most boats on Saturday and Sunday mornings. Plan a Saturday night and hit Damnoen Saduak on Sunday morning to catch both at full swing.

faq.q: Can you do this trip without your own car?
faq.a: You can, but the timing is tricky because the sights are spread out and Damnoen Saduak has to be done early. Hiring a private car or using local hired transport in stretches is the way to go; driving yourself is the smoothest and gives you the best control over timing.

faq.q: What's worth stopping for between Amphawa and Damnoen Saduak?
faq.a: Stop at Wat Luang Pho Sodh Dhammakayaram in Phaeng Phuai sub-district along the Bang Phae–Damnoen Saduak road, the Lao Tak Lak old original floating market, and — if you have time on the Samut Songkhram side — Wat Bang Kung with its bodhi-tree-wrapped chapel in Bang Khonthi.
